scope: Directions only; no product source or Cargo files changed in this Run.

directions.title: Bound Tokio to the dedicated SSE thread's actual workload
change_direction: In the workspace normal dependency, replace tokio features=["full"] with the direct xhm-desktop requirement set rt/sync/time/macros. Preserve transitive reqwest networking features selected by reqwest itself.
Inside the existing xhm-desktop-sse dedicated std::thread, replace tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread().worker_threads(2) with Builder::new_current_thread().enable_all().
Do not remove or change Slint accessibility in this first attempt. Do not merge renderer/window lifecycle changes into the same measurement.
behavior_to_preserve: Two independent SSE subscriptions remain live.
Floating resubscribe cancels and recreates only its active request.
Retry, cancellation, bounded channel backpressure, config probe, tray, and Slint event loop behavior remain unchanged.

expected_impact.qualitative: Removes two Tokio worker threads from the three-thread SSE arrangement and reduces direct Tokio feature/code surface. Some stack/control private commit and binary size reduction is expected, but no MiB value or <10 MiB pass is claimed before measurement.
expected_impact.target_assessment: Conservative first optimization only; a 23.5 MiB normal-state gap is too large to assume this change alone closes the gate.

verification: Run the local live dual-SSE fixture and verify both streams connect, receive heartbeats, resubscribe, cancel, and stop cleanly.
Repeat normal collapsed and XHM_DESKTOP_UI_SMOKE profiles with the same launcher, warmup, and 60 one-second samples.
Record binary hash/size, thread count, Private Bytes, VirtualQueryEx categories, and compare against this Run without changing another variable.
regression_tests: Windows release smoke for dual HWND, tray exit, taskbar placement, and dual SSE
directions.rollback: Revert the Tokio feature list and runtime builder together. Roll back immediately if either SSE stream starves, resubscribe/cancel ordering changes, shutdown hangs, or the measured reduction is too small to justify keeping the narrower runtime.
directions.success_boundary: Behavior remains P2-equivalent and Private Bytes decreases reproducibly. The P2 memory gate remains failed unless every acceptance sample is below 10 MiB.

directions.title: Restore Locked click transition parity
directions.change_direction: Change Rust panel_after_click so Expanded -> Locked, Locked -> Expanded, Clickthrough -> Clickthrough, and Collapsed remains Collapsed. The C# source of truth explicitly ignores Collapsed clicks.

expected_impact.behavior: Unlocking a locked panel returns to Expanded so pointer-leave can collapse it; collapsed clicks no longer lock without hover.

verification: Add/adjust transition tests for all four PanelState inputs.
Verify subscription remains Full across Locked -> Expanded and becomes Lite only after pointer leave collapses.
directions.rollback: Revert the transition table if C# parity or subscription state tests regress.

directions.title: Cap pinned-card viewport and keep overflow scrollable
directions.change_direction: Replace the uncapped pinned VerticalLayout with a capped ListView/viewport sized for at most four visible cards. Keep all pinned processes accessible by scrolling and derive the details panel offset/height from the capped viewport height rather than total pinned count.

expected_impact.behavior: Five or more pinned cards remain within the window and no longer drive the process-list panel to negative or clipped geometry.

verification: Render 0, 1, 4, 5, and 12 pinned rows in collapsed, Expanded, and Locked states.
Verify the first four are visible, overflow scrolls, unpin works, and the process ListView retains a positive bounded height.
directions.rollback: Restore the previous layout if scrolling or pin/unpin projection regresses; no data-model migration is involved.

directions.title: Clamp unsnapped drag release to monitor work area
directions.change_direction: When snap_floating_window returns None, clamp the current physical rectangle to the selected monitor's work_area and call move_topmost with the clamped origin before setting organic_state=floating. Preserve the existing 24 px edge snap path and physical-pixel/DPI conversion.

expected_impact.behavior: An unsnapped release cannot leave the floating window outside usable monitor bounds or under the taskbar.

verification: Add deterministic work-area clamp cases for each edge, oversized/off-screen coordinates, negative-origin monitors, and an already-valid rectangle.
On Windows, drag near but outside the snap threshold on monitors with taskbars on all four edges and verify physical RECT remains inside rcWork.
directions.rollback: Revert only the unsnapped else-branch clamp if multi-monitor placement regresses; the snap path stays unchanged.

ordering: Apply and measure FD-MEM-01 alone first. The three G3 parity directions are independent low-risk behavior repairs and must not be mixed into the memory attribution build.
